facts: Ryan Wang, Akshita Bhagia, and Sewon Min authored the paper 'EMO: Pretraining Mixture of Experts for Emergent Modularity', published on arXiv on May 7, 2026.
Standard Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models suffer severe performance degradation when inference is restricted to a subset of experts for a given domain.
EMO achieves modularity without human-defined priors by restricting tokens within a document to choose from a shared expert pool, while different documents use different pools.
EMO relies solely on document boundaries during pretraining to induce the emergence of coherent expert groupings.
The authors pretrained a 1B-active, 14B-total parameter EMO model on 1 trillion tokens.
As a full model, EMO matches the performance of standard MoE architectures.
Retaining only 25% of experts in EMO causes only a 1% absolute drop, and retaining 12.5% causes a 3% absolute drop, whereas standard MoEs break.
Unlike standard MoEs that exhibit low-level syntactic specialization, EMO expert subsets specialize at semantic levels such as math or code.
